title: Veridian Capital - first token pathway & security fit
summary: Intro discovery to scope Veridian's move from prototype to pilot. Discussed self-serve free credits and expected time-to-first-token, API ergonomics, and security constraints driving a likely dedicated or private pilot for PCI-style data. Agreed next steps: provide SOC2/HIPAA docs, share pricing and pilot SOW template, set up a sandbox project + sample benchmark instructions.
next_steps: Liam: email SOC2 and security pack by 2026-08-19
Rashida: create sandbox project + sample curl snippet and share by 2026-08-20
Tom/Aisha: confirm pilot data anonymization scope by 2026-08-21
Schedule technical deep dive (SE-led) week of 2026-08-24
action_items: Liam Park (AE) - Send SOC2, ISO, and compliance docs (due 2026-08-19)
Rashida Gomez (SE) - Provision sandbox org + sample benchmark script (due 2026-08-20)
Priya Menon (SecOps) - Provide list of required controls and KMS policy snippets (due 2026-08-21)
Tom Reynolds - Share representative dataset size and QPS target for pilot (due 2026-08-21)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-17 15:00 UTC / Duration 43m / Attendees: Liam P., Rashida G., Nora L. (Redwood) | Aisha K., Tom R., Priya M., Marco S. (Veridian)

00:00:03 Liam Park: Hey everyone thanks for carving time today, quick roll call, and we'll dig into how to get you from prototype to pilot.
00:00:12 Aisha Khan: Hi all - hi Liam, Rashida; thanks. we've been tinkering with a few models locally, hoping to move faster without writing ops. main ask is: how fast can we get a PoC that touches real data but is safe?
00:00:27 Liam Park: Totally, quick overview: Redwood offers the hosted API for fastest time-to-first-token, dedicated capacity for known throughput and data isolation, and private (VPC/on-prem) when you need stricter network control. Today we can map those to your constraints.
00:00:44 Tom Reynolds: By time-to-first-token do you mean literally from sign-up to first real API call? like minutes?
00:00:51 Rashida Gomez: Yes, for many teams it's minutes to an hour. With self-serve + free credits we usually see engineers getting a valid request in under 20 minutes — create org, API key, sample cURL or SDK, run a quick prompt. We'll share the exact snippet.
00:01:06 Priya Menon: but we can't send PII to a multi-tenant hosted endpoint unless we have legal/compliance coverage. so we need to understand data handling, retention, and key management.
00:01:17 Liam Park: Agreed. For sensitive data, customers typically go two ways: dedicated reserved pools where data is isolated at the tenancy level, or private deployment with customer VPC/on-prem where we don't see the traffic. Both can be part of the pilot.
00:01:32 Aisha Khan: Ok. what about costs for dedicated — rough ballpark? and how do free credits fit in — can we spin up the PoC on hosted with tokens and then transition?
00:01:42 Liam Park: Yes that's the common pattern. Start hosted under free credits to validate the integration and latency/quality; if you need isolation we sequence to Dedicated for throughput predictability, or Private for full network control. I'll send a pricing sheet but expect pilot-level reserved capacity options — we'll tailor it.
00:01:58 Marco Silva: From product POV, we want sub-second response for short summarization tasks, and embeddings for similarity. What's realistic on hosted vs dedicated?
00:02:10 Rashida Gomez: For short sequences, hosted with a low-latency model will be sub-second median for single-token generation plus streaming. Dedicated reduces variability and gives consistent p95s. Embeddings are generally cheap and fast; biggest lever is batching and KV cache behavior.
00:02:28 Tom Reynolds: You mentioned KV cache — we've been doing local cache tricks. any ops work to integrate?
00:02:34 Rashida Gomez: It's mostly automatic on the runtime side, but we can provide guidance. note the transcript: sometimes the model names get messed up in transcripts — K-V cash, K V cash — so apologies in advance.
00:02:46 Aisha Khan: Haha noted.
00:02:51 Speaker 1: (joined late) hello, sorry, had calendar overlap.
00:02:56 Liam Park: no worries. Quick question — who owns security at Veridian? Priya?
00:03:01 Priya Menon: yes. our bar: SOC2, SSO with SAML/Okta, KMS integration for key isolation, audit logs, and VPC peering for private link. Also retention controls — we can't keep raw customer PII after processing.
00:03:17 Liam Park: Understood. We support SAML/SSO, RBAC, per-tenant audit logs. For KMS options, we can integrate with your KMS via customer-managed keys for encryption at rest, and for private deployments keys remain in your vault. We'll include our standard security pack.
00:03:33 Aisha Khan: Great — does Redwood host SOC2 docs publically?
00:03:37 Liam Park: Yes — will attach SOC2 and a short security one-pager. For HIPAA/BAA that is a separate engagement; we can discuss if needed.
00:03:45 Tom Reynolds: Onboarding: what do we need to do to try the API? code samples, SDK?
00:03:51 Rashida Gomez: We have SDKs in Node/Python, but minimal cURL is enough. Typical quickstart: create org, create API key, run the sample request (we'll provide a sample chat and embeddings request). Should be <20 minutes for an engineer. We'll also provide a quick notebook for your data shape.
00:04:09 Marco Silva: Can you simulate production latency — our prod QPS is ~30 rps with spikes to 200. Does Redwood support burst?
00:04:18 Liam Park: Yes — on Hosted we have burst capacity but p95 variability higher. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and configurable autoscaling policies with burst buffers. For the pilot we often recommend a small dedicated pool if you expect steady high load.
00:04:33 Priya Menon: We also need VPC peering or private link options — we won't allow egress from our VPC without peering.
00:04:40 Rashida Gomez: Private deployment supports customer VPC and peering. For Dedicated we can set up private network options depending on region and account tier. We'll capture exact network requirements in the next steps.
00:04:53 Aisha Khan: If we start on hosted with real-ish data under free credits, how do we ensure retention controls e.g., short-term only and deletion after processing?
00:05:03 Liam Park: We have data retention flags and can set logs to minimal retention for pilot. Important: for full compliance we'd recommend dedicated or private where logs and data storage are isolated and can follow your retention policies. We'll show the retention config in the console.
00:05:17 Tom Reynolds: Any gotchas for SDKs or CORS when embedding in a UI prototype?
00:05:22 Rashida Gomez: For browser calls we recommend proxying through your backend to avoid exposing API keys. We also have guidance for secure token exchange and short-lived keys. We'll include sample patterns.
00:05:33 Speaker 1: Do you have streaming examples for partial results?
00:05:36 Rashida Gomez: Yes, streaming is supported across hosted and dedicated. For private deployments streaming works similarly but requires network considerations. We'll send sample JS and Python streaming snippets.
00:05:49 Aisha Khan: On instrumentation: can we get token-level cost and latency breakdown per route?
00:05:55 Liam Park: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdown and per-model latency dashboards. For pilot we'll share temporary access to console metrics.
00:06:06 Marco Silva: What about function-calling / structured outputs — we need to extract fields reliably for downstream processing. Any deterministic tool?
00:06:14 Rashida Gomez: We support structured output helpers and function-calling patterns; it's model dependent but we have evals and example prompt patterns. We'll include a small notebook showing field extraction stability over a sample prompt set.
00:06:27 Tom Reynolds: Competitors — is there anything you think we should watch out for vs other vendors?
00:06:31 Liam Park: Some vendors focus on pure model access but few offer unified runtime + ops controls like rollouts, cache, quantization recommendations. We often talk about latency/cost tradeoffs — you might see tradeoff floors from the big cloud endpoints.
00:06:44 Aisha Khan: Regarding pilot success criteria: what do you typically see?
00:06:48 Liam Park: Define perf (p95 < X ms), quality (on prompt tests or fuzz evals), and cost targets or unit economics per 1k requests. For Veridian I'd suggest pilot criteria: functional parity with local model, p95 latency target for summarization, and a cost estimate for 1 month at expected scale.
00:07:05 Priya Menon: We'll need audit logs for all developer/API activity during the pilot.
00:07:09 Liam Park: We'll enable audit logs and provide S3 export options if you prefer.
00:07:14 Marco Silva: Any constraints for multimodal? not in scope today but curious.
00:07:18 Rashida Gomez: We have growing multimodal support; for the pilot focusing on text + embeddings is easiest. Multimodal often has different infra profiles.
00:07:27 Aisha Khan: Ok let's talk timeline — we want to run a 2-3 week pilot as fast as possible. what's realistic?
00:07:33 Liam Park: If you start with hosted free credits today: day 0 to day 1 — create org and spike first calls; day 1 to day 3 — iterate on prompts and sampling; by week 1 you can have a baseline; move to a dedicated or private pilot in week 2 once security details are sorted.
00:07:48 Tom Reynolds: On the security pack — can you list the specific docs you'll send?
00:07:52 Liam Park: SOC2 report, security whitepaper, network architecture for private deployment, KMS integration notes, SSO/SAML guide, data retention section, and a pilot SoW template.
00:08:02 Priya Menon: Good. Also want to run a small benchmark with synthetic data to validate p95 at our target QPS.
00:08:08 Rashida Gomez: We'll provide a benchmark script and guidance on input shapes. We'll also include recommendations for batching, quantization profile you can consider later.
00:08:18 Aisha Khan: Quick note about the free credits — any restrictions on model family or throughput?
00:08:23 Liam Park: Free credits typically let you pick from the hosted model catalog; throughput for hosted sandbox is shared but fine for functional tests. If you need performance parity, the dedicated pilot will be required.
00:08:36 Tom Reynolds: Ok. Is there a sandbox that mirrors dedicated latency characteristics?
00:08:41 Rashida Gomez: We can provision a small dedicated-ish environment for pilot benchmarking, but it needs sign-off and minimal contract; otherwise hosted is shared and will show more variability.
00:08:52 Speaker 1: (inaudible) how about SSO onboarding? we use Okta.
00:08:56 Liam Park: SSO with Okta is supported. We'll include the SAML metadata exchange steps in the doc pack.
00:09:02 Marco Silva: For rollout — do we get canary and automatic fallback to smaller models if latency spikes?
00:09:09 Rashida Gomez: Yes, Rollouts in Redwood Console support canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies to compatible lower-cost or lower-latency variants. We can model policies for your traffic patterns.
00:09:21 Aisha Khan: Nice. Anything else we should be aware of from an infra perspective?
00:09:25 Liam Park: If you plan heavy caching of responses, avoid storing raw PII long-term; also watch KV cache warm-up for initial requests — we can share best practices.
00:09:36 Tom Reynolds: Let's talk about acceptance criteria for the pilot — would you help define those?
00:09:40 Liam Park: Absolutely. We'll draft a pilot SOW with success metrics: stability target, quality pass-rate on prompt evals, and a clear rollback path.
00:09:49 Aisha Khan: Great. Any legal procurement timing we should plan for?
00:09:53 Liam Park: For a small pilot we can use a streamlined agreement; enterprise contracts for Dedicated/Private add more time. We'll share a pilot SOW template for internal review.
00:10:04 Priya Menon: If we move to Private, what parts run in our network vs Redwood control plane?
00:10:11 Rashida Gomez: The private package separates control plane (optional) and data plane; for on-prem you'd own the data plane and key material. We'll detail the network flows.
00:10:22 Aisha Khan: Ok let's wrap with immediate next steps.
00:10:26 Liam Park: Recap: we'll send SOC2/security pack, sample cURL/SDK snippets, sandbox org, benchmark script, and a pilot SOW template. You'll confirm pilot scope and dataset and Priya will send required controls. Plan to meet the week of 2026-08-24 for a technical deep dive.
00:10:41 Tom Reynolds: Sounds good.
00:10:43 Marco Silva: Good, thanks team.
00:10:46 Liam Park: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email — talk soon.

[End of recording — remainder of call was wrap and scheduling notes]
notes: Transcript contains occasional transcription errors (model names, acronyms). Customer leaning to start hosted free credits for time-to-first-token, then move to dedicated/private for compliance. Agreed pilot SOW and security doc exchange.
